headline: Revenue dips as margin pressure drives a rare quarterly loss
summary_short: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell 1.7% y/y to $800.3M and gross margin compressed 230bp to 41.4% on new-Gallery occupancy costs, driving RH to a rare $13.7M net loss versus $8.0M of net income a year ago.
summary_long: Q1 FY2026 revenue fell 1.7% y/y to $800.3M on softer core/Contract demand, partly offset by hospitality growth from new Galleries. Gross margin fell 230bp to 41.4%, mainly on higher new-Gallery occupancy costs and weaker outlet/core product margins. SG&A as a % of revenue rose 440bp excluding a one-time $32M credit-card-interchange legal settlement, on higher compensation and pre-opening/advertising costs. RH swung to a $13.7M net loss (adjusted EBITDA margin 7.1%) from $8.0M of net income a year ago. Adjusted capex was $78M; FY2026 adjusted capex guidance is $240-260M. RH guides FY2026 revenue growth of 4.5%-8% and adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.2%-16%, including a 270bp drag from international pre-opening costs.

drivers.explanation: Revenue and gross margin both declined as core-business demand softened and new-Gallery occupancy costs rose ahead of their revenue contribution, driving a rare net loss; a $32M one-time legal settlement partly cushioned SG&A.
RH Segment revenue fell on lower core and Contract-business revenue, partially offset by higher hospitality revenue from new Gallery openings; Waterworks revenue also fell 1.7%.
Margin compression was primarily attributable to higher occupancy costs from new Gallery openings and decreased product margins in the RH outlet and core businesses.
Gross-margin compression outpaced the benefit of the $32M legal settlement and modest SG&A dollar savings, while pre-opening and advertising costs rose with new Gallery openings.
The swing to a net loss mirrors the operating-income decline; the equity-method line also flipped from an $8.2M gain (an Aspen LLC distribution) to a $0.4M loss.
